extracted.intended_audience: advocates, activists, policy shapers, researchers, communications practitioners, and social-change organizations
extracted.subtask_description: A methodology for researching, designing, testing, and mobilizing framing and narrative strategies to deepen public understanding, shift attitudes, and build support for social-change policies. Focuses on integrating social and cognitive science methods with collaborative engagement and iterative testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply rigorous social science methods
rubrics_metrics.description: We apply rigorous social science methods to study how people think about social issues and how we can communicate about them more effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical research methods (qualitative and quantitative) to discover how target audiences understand issues and which messages influence understanding and attitudes. FrameWorks emphasizes methodological rigor as foundational to effective communications work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage side-by-side with practitioners and communities
rubrics_metrics.description: We work side-by-side with social-change storytellers, organizations, and coalitions to leverage the power of evidence-based framing to advance progressive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborate directly with advocates, activists, policy shapers, researchers, and people with lived experience throughout research and implementation so findings are practice-ready and contextually grounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Frame Analysis® — answer four essential questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic Frame Analysis® is FrameWorks’ proprietary process for effective social-change communications research and practice—an evidence-based methodology that answers four essential questions that are integral to influencing public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The four essential questions are: (1) What's the story you want to tell? (2) What's the story being told? (3) What stories could work better? (4) How can you mobilize the new story to create change? Use this sequence to move from defining core ideas to diagnosing current narratives to designing/testing alternatives and planning implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify core ideas the public needs to understand
rubrics_metrics.description: We work with advocates, activists, policy shapers, researchers, and people with lived experience to identify a set of core ideas that the public needs to understand in order to fully grasp the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the 'big insights and perspectives' that should be represented in public conversations. The chosen core ideas should promote informed decision-making, reduce susceptibility to misinformation, and increase support for actions that lead to a more just and inclusive society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map cultural mindsets and document dominant narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: We map cultural mindsets, document dominant narratives, and explore recurring framing strategies used in the media, popular culture, and advocacy communications in order to understand the current stories being told and identify what needs to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct narrative and cultural analysis across media and advocacy channels to diagnose prevailing frames, metaphors, and assumptions that shape public thinking and to identify barriers to the desired framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate interdisciplinary theory and iterative methods to test frames
rubrics_metrics.description: We integrate methods and theory from across the social and cognitive sciences into a rigorous, iterative methodology designed to uncover effective framing and narrative strategies that deepen knowledge, shift attitudes, and build policy support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine cognitive science, social psychology, communications research, and experimental testing in cycles of design, testing, and refinement. Prioritize iterative evidence over intuition to identify messages that measurably improve understanding and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and support implementation strategies to mobilize new stories at scale
rubrics_metrics.description: We build strategies for implementing effective frames and narratives at the scale required to change thinking and increase understanding of the core ideas over time—and support our partners to use these strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop practical, scalable plans for getting new frames into public discourse (media, advocacy, coalitions) and provide partners with tools and support to deploy and sustain framing strategies so cultural mindsets shift over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use evidence-based framing to advance progressive change
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re on a mission to change conversations about social issues...to leverage the power of reframing to create a more just world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient framing work toward measurable social-change outcomes (e.g., increased policy support, reduced misinformation, greater public understanding). FrameWorks positions evidence-based reframing as a tool for advancing justice-oriented policy and practice.
